What happens to TLT if the 20Y and 30Y go to…

Fill in a target for each yield, or drag the sliders. Base point is the last day in the selected range.

Duration model: Δy = share × Δ20Y + (1 − share) × Δ30Y, then ΔP/P ≈ −D·Δy + ½·C·Δy² (Δy in percentage points). Duration and convexity default to iShares' figures for TLT. The 30% share on the 20Y comes from regressing TLT's daily returns on both yields over 6M to 5Y windows, which gives 24–28%; interpolating TLT's ~26-year average maturity between the two points gives ~40%.

Yield candles from CNBC market quotes; the scenario and the charts below use FRED's official daily closes, which can differ by a few bp and lag a day. TLT candles are Yahoo prices, not adjusted for distributions, so the price drops on each monthly ex-dividend day. History: TLT from its July 2002 launch; CNBC has the 20Y from 1994 and the 30Y from 1990, but some older days carry only a close and draw as flat dashes (the 20Y until the bond was reissued on 2020-05-20; the 30Y before 1997 and in patches to 2017).
